text:
maria: Heads up — p99 latency on dedicated-pool-7 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms around 10:14 UTC. Seen across multiple models, medium-seq workloads primarily. :eyes:

kai: saw the alert. Is this the KV-cache thrash we hit last month?

maria: initial flamegraphs point to a new kernel path being chosen frequently: the cuDNN fallback instead of the custom fast kernel. stack snippet from profiler:```
  runtime->launch_kernel: 85%
    cuDNN::conv_forward: 60%
    flash_kernel_stub: 5%
    wait on memcpy: 20%
```

sam: interesting — our kernel-selector logs show an upshift in memory pressure signals from that node group around the same time. selector decided for stability -> cuDNN on medium sequences.

leo: any noisy tenant index? devops-bot attached recent GPU usage heatmap:```
  host-7: tenant-a 62% gpu, tenant-b 18%, tenant-c 12%
  host-8: tenant-x 95% gpu (spike)
```

maria: tenant-x had a big batch job start at 10:12 and kept OOM retries. We also see KV cache evictions spike: `kv_evictions/s` from 5 -> 220 in 2m.

infra: that fits. When KV cache evicts heavily, batcher adjusts batching window (reduces prefetch) and selector sees reduced available GPU memory -> prefer cuDNN stability path. Result: higher latency.

kai: repro plan — run medium-seq perf with a synthetic noisy tenant that allocates persistent workspace to force fragmentation and KV thrash. I can spin up on canary.

maria: filesystem dump of process maps attached:```
  /opt/redwood/runtime/bin/runtime --args
  GPU mem free: 1.8GB -> 300MB during spike
  allocator fragmentation: 43%
```

nora: quick mitigation options: 1) pin kernel via env REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=fast_flash for affected pool, 2) throttle tenants with noisy job class, 3) bump reserved slots for dedicated-pool-7. Which do we want for an emergency patch? :zap:

sam: pinning kernel is quickest but risky if memory really low -> might OOM. Throttling noisy tenant is safe and immediate.

leo: I agree. I'll add a temporary quota on tenant-x and move its job to lower-priority queue. Doing now.

infra: while leo applies quota, let's check selector metrics. Kai, can you enable debug kernel-selector logs for the pool and capture a 15m window? `curl -X POST $OBS/api/debug?pool=dedicated-pool-7`

kai: enabled. logs will stream to /var/logs/selector/debug-1849102468.log. Also starting the synthetic repro.

maria: after throttling tenant-x, p99 dropped to ~160ms in next 2 minutes. still above baseline but much better. Looks like the kernel switch was the main driver.

sam: captured trace shows selector decision tree picking cuDNN when `usable_mem < 600MB` and `fragmentation > 30%`. Those thresholds were tuned last year — maybe needs revisiting for medium-seq distribution.

kai: repro results: with synthetic fragmentation we reproduce the switch consistently. With KV cache pinning (increase quota to avoid evictions) we keep the fast kernel and latency stays ~110-130ms.

maria: action items: 1) infra: keep tenant-x throttled until we have a safer autoscaling policy (leo) 2) eng-ml/kai: run a quick canary to test lowering selector threshold for fragmentation 3) prodops/sam: consider adding a soft-isolation knob to avoid eviction storms 4) create postmortem if this crosses SLA.

leo: quota applied and noisy job preempted. I'm leaving it throttled for 1h.

infra: scheduling a rollback window for selector threshold tweak. Kai, can you prepare a canary patch that reduces the fragmentation trigger from 30% -> 45% (i.e., be more tolerant) and run against two hosts?

kai: will do. running canary against host-7 and host-9 now, using debug build and capturing perf counters.

nora: small note — if we make selector more tolerant we risk OOMs under real fragmentation. Suggest also adding a fast fallback: if pinned kernel fails with OOM, auto-fallback to cuDNN and mark host unhealthy for 5m.

maria: good idea. let's implement the safe-fallback guard in the patch.

sam: I'll draft an incident blurb for customers and track SLA impact. so far error rates are unchanged, only latency P99.

maria: thanks everyone. Kai, update when canary finishes and attach selector debug log. We'll reconvene in the incident channel if canary shows regressions. :thumbsup:
